attempts.summary: Built dual-transit redundant path failover between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense), carrying traffic between node3's private network (10.10.10.0/24) and node4's private network (10.10.20.0/24). Configured the two transit links (10.10.1.0/30, 10.10.2.0/30) and both private links, then ran OSPF area 0.0.0.0 over both transit networks — FRR ospfd natively on VyOS, and the os-frr/Quagga plugin installed and configured on OPNsense — giving ECMP across both paths with automatic sub-second reroute on link failure. Demonstrated the required failover live twice: disabling transit-A (VyOS eth1) produced zero packet loss across 66 continuous pings between the private hosts, then disabling transit-B (OPNsense vtnet2) produced only 1 lost packet across 147 continuous pings, with OSPF reconverging to the surviving link both times and returning to dual-path ECMP on restoration. Diagnosed and fixed a real bug along the way: strict reverse-path filtering on node3/node4 silently dropped ICMP replies whenever OSPF ECMP hashed a flow onto the transit-IP-sourced path unfamiliar to the private hosts' routes; fixed by disabling rp_filter on the private interface, persisted via /etc/sysctl.conf. All node3/node4 IP and route config was persisted through /etc/network/interfaces.d so it survived the mandated reboots. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for all four nodes: captured pre-restart boot identity and health/data proof, issued each node's native reboot with the acknowledgement returning before disconnect, polled until each node's exec path returned, proved a changed boot identifier (VyOS boot_id, OPNsense kern.boottime, Ubuntu boot_id) on every node, and confirmed post-restart recovery of interface config, OSPF adjacency/ECMP, and end-to-end node3↔node4 reachability before moving to the next node.
